explainedBy: The anxious listener holds the two-column pros and cons page: putting the swirl of worry on paper is what calms him.

storyboard.claim: Writing the choice down is therapeutic and forces objectivity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener, still worried, holding the notes beside the two-column list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the legal-pad pros/cons method from the previous beats.
storyboard.addedInformation: The list is on screen as the thing that does the calming.

explainedBy: Same listener, same list: his face turns from worried to relieved, the list as an anxiety-reduction tool.

storyboard.claim: The pros/con list is an excellent anxiety reduction tool.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same listener with the list, now relieved.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; the face changes from worried to happy.
storyboard.addedInformation: The change of face shows the anxiety lifting.

explainedBy: Comparison: the written list beside the coin in his hand - the list beats a coin flip or a blind whim.

storyboard.claim: The list is better than flipping a coin or a blind emotional whim.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The list icon while the listener holds a coin.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Weighs the list against the alternative of chance.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the coin in hand shows the alternative; the comparison itself rests on the callout.

explainedBy: The turn: relying on the list as the ultimate tool is a trap - the listener slumps over the very list he trusted.

storyboard.claim: Johnson argues relying on the pros/con list as your ultimate tool is a dangerous trap.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener slumped and worried over the list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the praise of the list into a warning.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slump over the list shows the list itself is the problem.

explainedBy: Structure: the list forces a static binary - only two boxes, option A and option B.

storyboard.claim: The list forces the brain to evaluate a completely static binary choice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter with exactly two buckets: Option A, Option B.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows why the list is a trap: its structure.
storyboard.addedInformation: The two-bucket diagram makes the binary visible.

explainedBy: The two columns of the legal pad assume the options on the table are the only ones - the listener holds the page, nothing else in view.

storyboard.claim: The two-column structure assumes the current options are the only options.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener holding the two-column list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the binary diagram back to the pad that creates it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The two columns on the list are what limit the options.

explainedBy: Kept stage: the list does nothing to make new options - the listener slumps, stuck with the same page.

storyboard.claim: The moral algebra does nothing to help generate new options; it assumes the map is finished.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same listener and list; he slumps, sad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; the body slumps as the limit sinks in.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slump shows being stuck with only what is on the page.

explainedBy: Narrow band thinking: all his energy goes into weighing option A against option B on a scale.

storyboard.claim: Spending all your energy weighing option A against option B keeps you locked in narrow band thinking.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance scale beside the worried listener.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the list to the act of weighing two sides.
storyboard.addedInformation: The scale literally shows weighing two options.

explainedBy: The missed alternative: a third path straight ahead beside the two-way fork - the listener notices option C.

storyboard.claim: Weighing A against B blinds you to the fact you could invent option C.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The fork with a third dotted path; the listener surprised, pointing at it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From weighing two sides to seeing a third path.
storyboard.addedInformation: The third path on the fork shows the option the list hid.

explainedBy: Option C as an event: the listener takes the competitor's offer letter to his current boss and negotiates a raise.

storyboard.claim: Go back to your boss, leverage the competitor's offer, negotiate a 20% raise and keep your friend and commute.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener holding the offer letter, talking to his surprised boss.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows what option C could be.
storyboard.addedInformation: The letter in hand and the boss show leverage in a negotiation.

explainedBy: The list alone: by design it only scores what is already written, it does not find anything new.

storyboard.claim: A pros/con list is narrow by design: an evaluation tool, not a discovery tool.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The two-column list alone on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back from option C to the verdict on the list.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the list is shown; the distinction is carried by the label.

explainedBy: The order of work: discover the terrain, widen the map, and only then choose.

storyboard.claim: Before doing the algebra you have to discover the terrain and widen your map.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow: Discover terrain -> Widen map -> Choose.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The alternative to starting with the list.
storyboard.addedInformation: The flow shows choosing comes last.

explainedBy: The question as a search: the listener holds a magnifier, looking for the hidden terrain.

storyboard.claim: How do we build a better map and discover the hidden terrain?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener holding a magnifier, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Poses the question the next story answers.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the magnifier suggests searching; the question is in the label.

noVisual: A change of topic has no object; the walk marks the move to a new setting.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transition from the list to the CIA case.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: transition only.

explainedBy: A new place and time: the CIA analyst walks into a secure room in Langley, 2010.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the CIA case.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept room; the model and the official arrive.

explainedBy: The model is a detailed replica of a residential compound; the analyst explains it, the official reacts.

storyboard.claim: It is a meticulously crafted replica of a mysterious residential compound.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same model; analyst talking, Brennan surprised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; analyst now explaining, partner reacts.
storyboard.addedInformation: The model reads as a walled compound.

explainedBy: Where the real compound is: Abbottabad, Pakistan - they stare down at the toy walls.

storyboard.claim: The compound is in Abbottabad, Pakistan; they stare at tiny toy walls.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same model; the analyst staring, surprised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; adds the place name.
storyboard.addedInformation: The place name labels the model.

explainedBy: The analyst points at the model's walls, which in reality are 15 feet high with barbed wire.

storyboard.claim: The toy walls stand for real 15-foot walls topped with barbed wire.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Analyst pointing at the walled model with barbed wire.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; pointing at the walls.
storyboard.addedInformation: The model's drawn barbed wire matches the narration.

noVisual: No jeep icon; the detail is named in the callout.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; faces show the amazement.

explainedBy: Week after week the analyst examines the model with a magnifier to answer one question: is bin Laden inside?

storyboard.claim: Week after week they study the model to answer: is Osama bin Laden hiding inside?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Analyst examining the model with a magnifier; Brennan worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; the analyst now inspects.
storyboard.addedInformation: The magnifier over the model shows the search.

explainedBy: Not a quick look and a vote: the analyst keeps working beside the model with her notes, for months.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; magnifier swapped for working notes.

explainedBy: The method was building maps of the decision: the analyst explains her notes beside the model, the official taken aback by the time.

storyboard.claim: They spent nine months deliberately building maps.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Analyst talking with notes; Brennan surprised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; she now explains.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes and model together show mapping.

explainedBy: Mapping is more than the physical diorama: the analyst points past the model to the unseen variables on her notes.

storyboard.claim: Mapping a decision is not just building 3D dioramas; it is mapping unseen variables.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; closes the definition.
